question: Do the two selective cross-fitted response programs identify stable weight-readable subspaces inside the same eight native sites?
method: Deterministically refit both frozen rank-8 bases. Compare their principal-angle spectra sitewise. For attention sites compile Q coordinates through the exact head block of c_proj; for MLP sites pull Q back through Down to the bilinear hidden product. Verify each compiled contraction against direct response projection on the opposite target half.

predictions.pred_a_authority_split_hash_finiteness_a: Authorities, disjoint halves, basis hashes, finite tensors, and <=8 model forwards close.
predictions.pred_b_crossfit_subspaces_overlap: At least six of eight sites have mean squared principal cosine >=0.50 and every site >=0.20.
predictions.pred_c_attention_weight_contractions_clo: For all three attention sites and both fits, compiled c_proj-coordinate writes match direct projected writes at relative squared error <=1e-10.
predictions.pred_d_mlp_weight_contractions_close: For all five MLP sites and both fits, Down-pulled bilinear contractions match direct projected writes at relative squared error <=1e-10.
predictions.pred_e_crossfit_weight_maps_agree: After optimal orthogonal alignment, held-out compiled write cosine is >=0.80 for at least six sites and >=0.60 for every site.

decision: A pass licenses literal projected-weight interfaces and fresh/OOD testing. Operational-equivalence-only retains causal usefulness but forbids treating one fitted coordinate basis as a stable weight circuit.
